action: use actix_web::{post, web, App, HttpResponse, HttpServer, Responder}; use serde::Deserialize; use std::fs::File; use std::io::{self, BufReader, Read}; use std::path::{Path, PathBuf}; use actix_web::http::header::ContentType; #[derive(Deserialize)] struct SongRequest { filename: String, } fn sanitize_filename(filename: &str) -> Option { // Basic sanitization to prevent directory traversal attacks if filename.contains("..") || filename.contains("/") || filename.contains("\\") { None } else { Some(filename.to_string()) } } #[post("/download")] async fn download_song(song_request: web::Json) -> impl Responder { let sanitized_filename = match sanitize_filename(&song_request.filename) { Some(name) => name, None => return HttpResponse::BadRequest().body("Invalid input"), }; let song_path = PathBuf::from(format!("/var/songs/{}", sanitized_filename)); // Check if the file exists if !song_path.exists() { return HttpResponse::NotFound().body("File does not exist"); } // Attempt to read the file let file = File::open(&song_path); match file { Ok(file) => { let mut reader = BufReader::new(file); let mut buffer = Vec::new(); match io::copy(&mut reader, &mut buffer) { Ok(_) => HttpResponse::Ok() .content_type(ContentType::audio_mpeg()) .body(buffer), Err(_) => HttpResponse::InternalServerError().body("Error reading file"), } } Err(_) => HttpResponse::InternalServerError().body("Error opening file"), } } #[actix_web::main] async fn main() -> std::io::Result<()> { HttpServer::new(|| { App::new() .service(download_song) }) .bind("0.0.0.0:5000")? .run() .await }

Additionally, the lack of validation for the `filename` input raises the risk of directory traversal attacks, compromising security.

The Safety Critic emphasizes the security vulnerabilities associated with the unvalidated `filename` parameter, which could allow unauthorized access to files outside the designated directory. Furthermore, the potential for Denial of Service (DoS) attacks due to excessive memory consumption when handling large files is a critical concern.
